title: Integrity wall-clock + cost audit — week-1 PROP-101 data shows integrity runs at 3931 seconds = ~65 minutes per run on Sonnet, $4.24/run. That's enormous for what should be a deterministic structure check. Audit what's eating the wall-clock, identify Haiku-able sub-steps vs Sonnet-required steps, propose Phase 0 measurement + Phase 1 split-or-slim if a clear lever exists.
context:
Week-1 cost-history.jsonl analysis (2026-06-14 → 2026-06-20):

  Agent       $/run    runs   $/week  avg_dur_sec   composition
  integrity   $4.24       5    $21    3931s (~65m)  29% write, 56% read, 15% out
  social      $3.02       4    $12    2390s (~40m)
  decider     $7.01       9    $63    2442s (~41m)  30% write, 52% read
  poller      $2.44       4    $10    5366s (~89m)
  workspace-  $2.18      41    $89    507s   (~8m)
  curmudgeon  $11.62     12    $139   821s   (~14m)

Integrity is the second-slowest agent by wall-clock (after poller's 89min, which is web-fetch-dominated). For a structure check on a known-shape repo, 65 minutes is striking.

What integrity actually does per the prompt: check 1 (#anchor resolution), 1b (relative-href resolution, added 2026-06-18), 2 (tab structure), 3 (external link validation — priority data sources only, doi.org excluded), 4 (data-prose consistency), 5/5b/5c/5d (WIN detail / dome alignment / progressive disclosure / hardcoded colors), 6 (discoverability), 7/7a/7a.5/7a.6 (expansion tracker continuity / ISS ID collision / FUSE staleness), 7b/7c/7d/7e/7f (workspace-only files / section-new coupling / workspace-sync skips / curmudgeon digest / broken review files), 7g/7h/7i (drift audit / Mech-A-bypass / curmudgeon dispatcher state precompute), 8 (project docs), 9 (build reproducibility).

The checks are heterogeneous — some are mechanical (anchor resolution, file existence, count consistency, hash comparison) and would be fine on Haiku; some are semantic / cross-reference (data-prose consistency, ISS collision audit, drift attribution) and probably want Sonnet. Today everything runs on the same Sonnet pass at $4.24/run.

Other-side check the operator already considered:
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Integrity runs daily — \$21/week is not the line item to optimize.' Counter: \$21/week is $1100/year for a check that fires once per day. Most of that 65-minute wall-clock is presumably mechanical work that Haiku does for 10% the cost. The savings ROI is moderate but real, and the slim/split would also reduce integrity's apparent-delay on flaggings (today integrity finds a real problem at 01:15Z but operator doesn't see it until run completes ~02:20Z).
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Integrity check correctness matters more than cost.' Counter: agree, which is why this is propose-only and any split must preserve all check coverage. A Haiku sub-check for mechanical work followed by a Sonnet summary review is conservatively safer than a single Sonnet pass — Haiku makes fewer judgment errors on mechanical checks because they ARE mechanical.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Splitting integrity adds complexity.' Counter: PROP-038 already split curmudgeon into discovery + verify (mode B). Same pattern. Worked.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Integrity already runs the dispatcher-state precompute (PROP-021) and drift-audit (PROP-020) — those moved most of the mechanical work into scripts.' Counter: those covered curmudgeon's mechanical work, not integrity's. Integrity still walks docs/index.html (4.5MB HTML), wins.json (200KB), sections.json (large), 700+ curmudgeon reviews, etc. There's room for additional script-level precompute and prompt-level slim.
task: Investigate integrity's per-check wall-clock + cost composition. Map which checks are mechanical (script-able / Haiku-able) vs semantic (Sonnet-required). Propose Phase 0 measurement + Phase 1 either (a) split into a Haiku mechanical pre-pass + Sonnet semantic-summary pass, or (b) extract more mechanical work into scripts that the LLM consumes (precompute artifacts, mirroring PROP-020 drift-audit / PROP-021 dispatcher-state). Honor the constraint that ALL check coverage must be preserved — this is a cost engineering exercise, not a coverage reduction.
investigation_questions: Q1 — Per-check token + wall-clock attribution. Add cheap STEP_MARKER instrumentation (mirror PROP-104 Phase 0's pattern) to integrity's structure-integrity.md major check headings (Check 1 through Check 9 + subchecks). Capture 3-5 runs. Surface the top-3 checks by token cost AND top-3 by wall-clock seconds. The two rankings may differ — wall-clock includes external HTTP calls (Check 3), token cost is dominated by the prompt prefix.

Q2 — Mechanical vs semantic classification. For each check, classify: (a) MECHANICAL (file exists / count matches / anchor resolves / hash matches — could be a script or Haiku), (b) SEMANTIC (cross-reference judgment — needs Sonnet), (c) MIXED (mechanical scan with semantic interpretation — could be split). Reference: drift-audit (PROP-020) was MECHANICAL and moved fully to script. ISS-ID collision check is MECHANICAL. External link validation is MECHANICAL (HTTP status). Data-prose consistency MIXED. Mech-A-bypass audit MIXED.

Q3 — Haiku eligibility per check. For each MECHANICAL check, would Haiku produce the same output as Sonnet does today? Smoke-test rationale: run Haiku-as-integrity on 1-3 historical integrity reports and compare findings against the Sonnet runs. If Haiku catches the same findings, that's evidence Haiku is sufficient for those checks. (Haiku at 0.1x the read cost = ~10x savings on the input-token-heavy checks.)

Q4 — Precompute extraction candidates. PROP-020 set the precedent (drift-audit precompute), PROP-021 extended it (curmudgeon-dispatcher-state). Both produced a deterministic JSON the LLM consumes in seconds. Candidate integrity precomputes: (a) anchor-resolution-report.json (Check 1 mechanical output), (b) relative-href-resolution-report.json (Check 1b mechanical output — the script we already shipped in this directive's commit), (c) data-prose-counts.json (Check 4 mechanical output), (d) external-link-status.json (Check 3 mechanical output, cacheable with TTL). Each precompute = (LLM-prose pages of check logic) — (small JSON consumption) tokens saved.

Q5 — Split into two-agent pipeline. Mirror PROP-038's curmudgeon split (discovery + verify). Could integrity become integrity-mechanical (Haiku, fast, computes the precomputes + flags every-issue-no-judgment) + integrity-semantic (Sonnet, reads the precompute summaries + applies judgment on cross-references)? Risk: handoff complexity. Benefit: per-component cost ~$0.50/run for Haiku + $2/run for Sonnet = $2.50/run vs today's $4.24 = 40% reduction. Plus wall-clock reduction.

Q6 — External link cadence. Check 3 (external link validation — NOAA, NASA, ESA, etc.) makes ~30 HTTP calls per run. At 15s timeout × some retry budget, that's a meaningful chunk of the 65-min runtime. Could external links be checked LESS often than daily — say, every 7 days OR only when a data file URL changes? The data sources don't disappear randomly. ESA's URL just permanent-redirected 2026-06-19 — that's a once-every-many-months event. Weekly cadence catches that within reasonable latency.

Q7 — Compare to curmudgeon-verify. curmudgeon-verify runs at 511s ($1.75/run) on Sonnet — sibling agent doing mechanical verification of patches. Integrity is 3931s ($4.24/run). The 8× wall-clock multiplier may be partly because integrity has more checks (~25 vs verify's ~5) but also probably partly because integrity hasn't been optimized. Map the per-check fixed overhead to estimate how much of the 65min is structural vs slimable.

Q8 — Will splitting break the 'integrity speaks with one voice' property? Today's integrity report is a single JSON with overall_status + issues_found[]. If split, integrity-mechanical's output is consumed by integrity-semantic which writes the final report. The operator's downstream consumers (decider Priority 2b, tinker Mode 1) read the final report — so the contract is preserved. The split is operationally invisible if done right. Acknowledge any edge cases (e.g. integrity-semantic crashes before writing the final report — mechanical findings are then lost unless the script writes them too).
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with: (1) Q1 per-check token + wall-clock attribution; (2) Q2 mechanical/semantic classification of all integrity checks; (3) Q3 Haiku eligibility per check with smoke-test results; (4) Q4 precompute extraction candidates with token-savings estimates; (5) Q5 two-agent split analysis with cost + risk; (6) Q6 external link cadence proposal; (7) Q7 comparison to curmudgeon-verify; (8) Q8 single-voice property preservation plan. Phased rollout: Phase 0 = measurement + script precompute shadow; Phase 1 = either model split OR additional precompute (whichever the Phase 0 evidence supports). Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
constraints: Preserve ALL integrity check coverage. The 9-check structure + subchecks must remain. Cost reduction must come from script-extraction or model-split, NOT from removing checks.

Honor the 'integrity speaks with one voice' contract. Downstream consumers (decider, tinker) read a single report-*.json and a single latest-integrity-summary.txt. Any split must produce these same outputs at the same paths.

Don't propose moving integrity to a different schedule cadence without an explicit justification. Today's 02:00 UTC daily cadence is what the rest of the pipeline depends on (decider's 02-slot reads it).

Haiku-eligibility claims must be backed by smoke-test evidence, not assumption. Q3 says 'run Haiku-as-integrity on historical reports and compare.' Do that comparison before recommending Haiku for any check.
Mirror PROP-020 / PROP-021 / PROP-038 patterns where they fit. Precompute artifacts produced by scripts + LLM consumes summaries. Split agent into discovery + verify if cost-benefit clears the bar.

related_prop_lineage: PROP-020 (drift-audit script precompute pattern). The first integrity precompute extraction. Set the pattern this directive's deliverable should mirror.

PROP-021 (curmudgeon dispatcher-state precompute + prompt slim). Same precompute-and-slim shape applied to a different agent. Stage 1 shipped, Stage 2 still pending observation per yesterday's analysis.
PROP-038 (curmudgeon discovery + verify split). The operational precedent for splitting a single agent into mechanical + semantic passes. Worked.
PROP-104 Phase 0 (STEP_MARKER instrumentation). The cheap measurement tool this directive's Q1 should apply directly.
PROP-101 (cost-history instrumentation). The data source motivating this directive.
background_artifacts.expected_ROI: If Phase 1 ships a Haiku/Sonnet split or substantial precompute extraction, conservative estimate is 30-50% cost reduction ($1.30-2.10/run savings → $470-770/year). Plus wall-clock reduction freeing operator review latency.

not_in_scope: Removing integrity checks. This is cost engineering, not coverage reduction.
Changing integrity's daily cadence without a rescue-latency analysis. Daily is what decider's 02-slot depends on.
Integrity prompt rewrite for narrative style. Cost is in the per-check work, not the prose framing.
Cross-agent precompute sharing (e.g., integrity + curmudgeon-verify share a precompute lib). Separate question if duplication emerges.
closure_note: operator ratify-close 2026-07-04: PROP-111 phase-0-and-1a-shipped (integrity precompute + cadence delivered)
